answer: Semantic Similarity Pairing with Mutual Slashing: each miner's response is embedded and only dissimilar answers get paired across a bridge of tasks. A pigment of shared phrasing flags cloned agents; the mirror check compares embeddings, and near-duplicates trigger mutual slashing of both stakes. An attacker cloning one model across 50 nodes pays 50 stakes and loses all 50 the moment similarity exceeds threshold, so the cost scales linearly while detection scales faster. This works because duplication is cheap to produce but detectable and self-punishing.
